handoff: Truth check: 5 blocking prose/code contradictions — T9 cursor source is by record policy (human.ts:132), T5b/D10 restart fallback vs restartStepOf, R3.4 'only', limitations/recipes 'record lost' ignores the open-pr push, concepts 'never in git'. Lint change and the rest verified; tests green.

findings.title: T9: the sender picks the cursor by record policy, not by whether a ref exists
findings.detail:
T9 says the sender stamps step/attempt 'from the run-state ref when there is one, else only the step the last boundary commit led to (Norn-Next)'. packages/cli/src/runtime/human.ts:132-140 (remoteTarget) does something else. Under `local`, the boundary's Norn-Next comes first even when a ref exists (one is pushed at every release and at open-pr), and the ref is read only when no Norn-Next boundary is found. Under `remote`, only the ref is read, with no Norn-Next fallback. The step-only path also covers the story unit only (slice -> branch null). D17 states this correctly ('A local non-holder ... Under remote the sender stamps step and attempt from the fetched ref').
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Reword T9 per policy as D17 does: under local, a story unit gets the Norn-Next step with no attempt (falling back to the ref when no such boundary exists); under remote, step and attempt come from the ref.

findings.title: T5b and spec D10: restart fallback differs from restartStepOf
findings.detail:
T5b says: Norn-Next, or Norn-Step only for a boundary an older norn made, 'when that workflow has it, else at the workflow's first step'. packages/core/src/apply.ts:65-67 `for (const at of [last?.next, last?.ended]) if (at && stepOf(wf, at)) return at;` also falls back to the ended step (Norn-Step) when Norn-Next is present but the workflow lacks it, e.g. `$done` or a step another round's workflow does not have. The JSDoc at apply.ts:60-64 agrees with the rule, so either the code or the rule (and D10, spec.md) is wrong.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Settle which behaviour is intended. Then change the rule and D10 to 'Norn-Next, else Norn-Step, whichever the workflow has', or open a code fix in a behaviour slice.

findings.title: R3.4: 'only' is false for run state and spec sources
findings.detail:
The rewritten R3.4 says run state is read 'only from the machine dir (S12) or, for a finished story, its run-state ref'. packages/store/src/snapshot.ts:209-213 also reads an older norn's runs/ from a worktree's branch tree (readUnit ... tree: true, B34 migration). The spec is also read from repoRoot for solo repos and unpushed stories (snapshot.ts:7, :354).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Name the older norn's branch runs/ (read until the B34 move) and the repo-root case, or drop 'only'.

findings.title: 'a holder that dies without releasing loses the run record' is false once the PR is open
findings.detail:
packages/cli/src/runtime/act/git-step.ts:20-31 (linkRecord) pushes the record before every PR open or update, under `local` too. After that, a takeover finds a record on the ref and resumes from that stale record (checkout.ts:396-405: maybeLost only when nothing was prepared). It does not restart from the last boundary with fresh counters. The record is lost only when nothing was ever pushed. docs/recipes.md:105 has the same flaw: its parenthetical '(local ... and your machine never released the claim)' is offered as the condition for having no record on the ref.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Say what is lost: everything after the last record push (a release or a PR open/update). The takeover then resumes from that older record, or, when nothing was ever pushed, restarts from the branch.

findings.title: 'Nothing in a worktree or in git holds it' / glossary 'never in git' contradict the record ref
findings.detail:
concepts.md:94 and the glossary row at :145 say run state is never in git. The next paragraph and the `record` row say it is packed into refs/norn/runs/<story>, a git ref (packages/store/src/record-ref.ts:141-167).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: 'No branch holds it' / 'never on a branch; archived to its record ref'.

findings.title: R3.2/T7b name only status: done; decide also blocks dropped
findings.detail:
packages/core/src/decide/story.ts:82 `baseDone = story.base_status === "done" || story.base_status === "dropped"`. The rewritten R3.2 (and T7b at :378) names only done. This is an omission, not a contradiction.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: 'status: done or dropped'.

findings.title: S4: 'Norn-Step (once the unit has a cursor)' holds only for decide's commits
findings.detail:
Runtime commits always carry a stand-in step: act/lifecycle.ts:76 `a.state?.step ?? "start"`, release.ts:57 `?? "release"`, checkout.ts:550 `"take"`, close.ts:55.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Drop the parenthetical, or say that a commit with no cursor carries the action's name.

findings.title: remote policy pushes on every tick whose packed record changed, not only at step boundaries
findings.detail:
packages/core/src/decide/story.ts:178-187 pushes when the packed tree differs from the ref. That happens on more than step boundaries.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: 'whenever the record changed (at least every step boundary)'.

findings.title: upgrade pointer lasts until the removal is on the base branch, not until it is committed
findings.detail:
baseRunStateStories(baseRoot ?? repoRoot) reads the fetched base tree (packages/store/src/snapshot.ts:126, :336, :358). With a fetched base, status/doctor keep pointing to upgrade until the removal is merged to the base. In the same sentence, '.gitattributes' is dropped once any story moved (commands/upgrade.ts:216-219), not per story. A record that fails validation also keeps its run state (record-ref.ts:519). Archiving covers every spec folder with runs/, not only finished stories (record-ref.ts:460-474).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: 'until that removal reaches the base branch'; 'per story' rather than 'per finished story'; mention the validation failure.

findings.title: Out of diff: repo workflow instructions still say a dev build acts on the worktree's runs/
findings.detail:
.agents/workflows/quick.yaml:36 and reproduce.yaml:18 say 'NORN_HOME points at it ... act on its runs/'. Run state is now in the machine dir, and NORN_HOME is the main checkout (act/session.ts:51). The slice updated AGENTS.md's matching sentence but not these.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Apply the same wording as AGENTS.md (B38 covers the docs set; the workflows are agent instructions).

findings.title: T7a/R2.3 say 'this checkout released'; the check is per machine (Norn-Holder user@host)
findings.detail:
packages/store/src/superseded.ts:77-80 compares Norn-Holder to machine holder. D11's remote caveat (a takeover without release whose receipts were all pushed is removed quietly) is not stated in T7a.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: 'this machine'; state the remote caveat.

findings.title: Launcher '~/.norn/launch/<hash>.sh, one per machine': one per PATH hash
findings.detail:
packages/cli/src/runtime/shim.ts:57 keys the launcher by a hash, so a machine can have several.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: 'one per PATH'.

findings.title: The record layout given does not hold for records archived from an older norn
findings.detail:
norn upgrade packs those as they were: _story/ with no rounds/, possibly with old handoff.md files.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add 'records an older norn left may lack rounds/'.

findings.title: UNIT_HANDOFF slug is looser than the slice name parser
findings.detail:
`[0-9]{2,}-[^/]+` accepts handoffs/1234-Foo Bar.md and handoffs/01-.md, which SLICE_FILE_RE (ids.ts:182, `[0-9]{2,3}-[a-z0-9-]+`) rejects. OLD_HANDOFF still passes any handoff.md under any runs/ in a spec folder (unchanged from before). The new rule is not too strict: unitHandoffPath (ids.ts:240) produces only names it accepts.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Use `[0-9]{2,3}-[a-z0-9-]+`.

findings.title: Test title 'every doc but the rules' overstates the scope
findings.detail:
allDocs leaves out .agents/specs/** (correctly, since those are history). The RULES.md exclusion is narrow: endsWith('.agents/RULES.md') (test/support/docs.ts:26).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: 'every doc in the doc set but the rules'.
